final.title: Design seasonality around one recurring workflow
final.body:
If you run a small business, seasonality stops being abstract when you pin it to one workflow that always gets noisy at the same time each year. For many owners, that is customer replies, fulfilment updates, invoicing, or lead follow-up. The useful question is not whether AI is fashionable. It is which repeatable task becomes the bottleneck first.

Start with the task you already feel in peak season: the one you handle manually, the one that makes you delay replies, or the one that tempts you to hire temporary help. Write down what that slowdown costs you in time and what good would look like in plain English: faster response, less backlog, or fewer hours spent on admin.

Then test the boundary. Can the work be split into a rule-based part and a judgment part? FAQs, invoice generation, and lead qualification can often be written as rules. High-stakes decisions, custom exceptions, and anything that needs careful human approval should stay with you. That line matters.

Next, check where the work already lives. If it is in email, a CRM, a spreadsheet, or another SaaS tool you already use, it is a cleaner candidate for a bounded automation pilot. If it does not repeat cleanly, or it depends on sensitive judgment, keep it manual or hire. Both are honest answers.

A practical next step: spend 10 minutes documenting one peak-season task, including inputs, rules, output, and how often it repeats. That gives you a clearer build-versus-hire decision before you think about tools.
